text.p: Temporary work agency BIS expects a fairly significant loss for 1996, which partly explains the 490 franc per share prce offered by Dutch Vendex International, finance director Michel Suhard said.

"The 1996 accounts have not yet been closed but due to a certain numbre of elements, mainly the fall in sales and the neagtive impact of the CFC (Caisse Fonciere de Credit) loans, we can say that the result will be negative in a rather significant way," Suhard told a news conference.

Claude Charbonniaud, who became chairman to replace founder Laurent Negro who died late in December, said that it would be on the basis of the 1996 results information that minority shareholders could decide whether or not to sell to Vendex.
Vendex agreed with the Negro family to acquire its 59.04 percent stake in BIS and plas a buy-out bid on the remaining 40.96 percent listed.
Vendex management board member Obe Kuipers said that this bid could take place in February, after permission by the European Union competition authorities.
